source.citation: Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation and Ethnological Museum Berlin, and Atlas Obscura. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Ngonnso' statue donated to the Berlin museum

attributes.summary: The German colonial officer Kurt von Pavel took the statue from Kumbo and donated it to the Ethnological Museum in Berlin. The Nso' say it was taken by force.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Ngonnso (CC BY-SA 4.0). Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.summary: After research, a female figure in the Ethnological Museum in Berlin-Dahlem was confirmed to be Ngonnso', and the Nso Palace was informed.

source.citation: Quartz Africa, Wikipedia, Ngonnso (CC BY-SA 4.0), and news reports on the Humboldt Forum. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.summary: Activist Sylvie Njobati, a member of the Nso people, launched the #BringBackNgonnso campaign in May 2021. In December 2021 representatives of the Nso community in Cameroon and Germany, German museum officials and scholars met to discuss the statue's provenance and significance.
attributes.museum_label: In Berlin the statue was described as a palm wine vessel.
attributes.reason: The Nso say they have suffered calamities since the statue was taken.

source.citation: Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation press release of 27 June 2022, and Reuters. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Foundation clears the way for Ngonnso' to return

attributes.summary: The board of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation decided to return Ngonnso' to Cameroon, the first restitution to Cameroon. It said the statue was not removed from Kumbo through war looting, but that the visit took place amid unequal power and colonial violence. It also announced the return of 23 pieces to Namibia.
attributes.significance: The foundation recognised Ngonnso's spiritual importance to the Nso as a mother deity.

source.citation: Open Restitution Africa case study, Wikipedia, Ngonnso (CC BY-SA 4.0), and TRT Afrika (21 January 2025). Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.status: The statue had not been physically returned in the most recent sources I found, from early 2025. The formal return had been authorised in 2022. I found no report of a physical return since.
attributes.obstacle: Despite announcements and symbolic handover ceremonies, a case study says it had not yet been repatriated to the State of Cameroon.
attributes.caution: Check current news, because this may have changed.
